22.4 Pesticides

Pesticides are chemicals that are used to destroy, repel or otherwise lower pest infestations to protect crops from damage or simply we can say a substance that kills a pest (insect, weed, bacteria, nematode etc.), for example lead arsenate, Pb₃(AsO₄)₂, nicotine sulphate etc.

An ideal pesticide should possess the following characteristics:

It should be effective only against the specific target organism.

It should be non-toxic to other living organisms.

It should be non-persistent.

It should be biodegradable.

It should break down in nature into harmless products and cause no damage to environment.

DDT براہِ راست کیڑوں پر عمل کرتی ہے۔ یہ بہت پائیدار کیمیکل ہے، اس کی نصف عمر کا اندازہ 10 – 15 سال ہے۔ DDT پانی میں ناحل پذیر ہے اس لیے یہ جانوروں میں اور خاص طور پر ان کی چربی والی بافتوں میں جمع ہوتی ہے۔ اسی لیے ماحولیات کے ماہرین نے دنیا میں DDT کے استعمال پر پابندی لگا دی۔

جدول 22.1 ځینې عام کروموفور ګروپونه

اوکسوکرومونه عموماً ’د رنګ مرستیالان‘ یا ’د رنګ ټینګوونکي‘ بلل کېږي. اوکسوکروم، د رنګ هغه برخه چې د رنګېدونکې مادې (معمولاً ټوکر) سره یې نښلوي، –NH₂، –OH، –NR₂، –COOH او –SO₃H ګروپونه دي. –NH₂ او –NR₂ په اسیدونو کې حلېدنه رامنځته کوي، په داسې حال کې چې –OH، –COOH او –SO₃H په قلوي محلولونو کې حلېدنه رامنځته کوي.

i. طبیعي رنګونه   ii. مصنوعي رنګونه

i. طبیعي رنګ

طبیعي رنګونه هغه رنګونه یا رنګوونکي دي چې له بوټو، بې ملا تیر ژویو یا منرالونو اخیستل کېږي. ډېری طبیعي رنګونه له نباتي سرچینو لکه ریښو، بېریو، پوستکي، پاڼو او لرګي څخه نباتي رنګونه دي. نورې عضوي سرچینې پوڅکي او لایکنونه دي.

Chemical Composition of a Dye

A dye consists of a colour producing structure called the ‘chromogen’ and a part to regulate the solubility and dying properties called the ‘auxochrome’. The chromogen is an aromatic body containing a colour-giving group, commonly called the ‘chromosphore’. Chromophore is that part of the molecule which when exposed to visible light will absorb and reflect a certain colour. Some common chromophores are given in the Table 22.1.

Table 22.1 Some Common Chromophore Groups

Auxochromes are commonly called as ‘colour helpers’ or ‘colour intensifiers’. The auxochrome, the part of the dye which causes it to adhere to the material which it colours (usually textiles) are –NH₂, –OH, –NR₂, –COOH and –SO₃H of these groups. –NH₂ and –NR₂ cause solubility in acids while –OH, –COOH and –SO₃H cause solubility in basic solutions.

Classification of Dye: There are several ways for classification of dyes. One of the prominent ways of classification is the classification based on the source of materials. It is further divided into two main types:

i. Natural Dyes ii. Synthetic Dyes

i. Natural Dye

Natural dyes are dyes or colorants derived from plants, invertebrates, or minerals. The majority of natural dyes are vegetable dyes from plant sources e.g. roots, berries, bark, leaves and wood. Other organic sources include fungi and lichens.

ii. Synthetic Dyes

Almost all the colours in use today are synthetic dyes. Synthetic dyes are used everywhere in everything from clothes to paper, from food to wood. This is because they are cheaper to produce, brighter, more colour-fast and easy to apply to fabric. For example, acid dyes, azo dyes, basic dyes, mordant dyes, etc.

Tidbit — Differences between dyes and pigments

Dyes and pigments are substances that impart colour to a material. The major difference between dyes and pigments is the particle size. Dyes are much finer than pigments. Dyes, also known as colourants in which the colouring matter is dissolved in liquid, are absorbed into the material to which they are applied. Pigments, on the other hand, consist of extremely fine particles of ground colouring matter suspended in liquid which forms a paint like film that actually bonds to the surface.

22.4 Pesticides

Pesticides are chemicals that are used to destroy, repel or otherwise lower pest infestations to protect crops from damage or simply we can say a substance that kills a pest (insect, weed, bacteria, nematode etc.), for example lead arsenate, Pb₃(AsO₄)₂, nicotine sulphate etc.

Characteristics of an Ideal Pesticide

An ideal pesticide should possess the following characteristics:

It should be effective only against the specific target organism.

It should be non-toxic to other living organisms.

It should be non-persistent.

It should be biodegradable.

It should break down in nature into harmless products and cause no damage to environment.

It should be inexpensive and easily available.

Pesticides are the chemical substances that are used to control the pests such as DDT, heptachlor etc. DDT has the formula,

DDT acts directly on insects. It is a very stable chemical, it’s half-life is estimated to be 10 – 15 years. DDT is insoluble in water, therefore, it accumulates in animals and in particular in their fatty tissues. Therefore, the environmentalists banned the use of DDT in the world.

Nowadays, parathion is used instead of DDT.
